The full name of the project is “Remembering the Waters: Co-creating Kenya’s Maritime and Inland-Water Safety Heritage Archive for Equity, Memory, and Future Transitions”. It works with coastal communities, Lake Victoria communities, survivors and families affected by past incidents, women in fishing communities, youth and informal transport workers, and with safety regulators, heritage institutions and universities.
The archive is run by the project team with the support of its funders and partner organisations, and it exists because of the people who have trusted it with their stories.

This policy explains what personal data the archive collects, why, how it is protected and what your rights are. It follows Kenya’s Data Protection Act, 2019.
From Contributors: the name, email address and picture supplied by Google or Apple when you sign in; the username and picture you choose; your language and settings.
What you post: stories, files, comments, reactions, messages, reports and safety concerns.

From everyone: basic technical records (pages opened, device type, approximate region from the internet address) used to keep the service safe and to count visits. Visitors are counted without identifying them.
From admins: name, work email, phone number, staff number and, if given, an ID or passport number, which is stored encrypted.

To run the archive, show your stories as you choose, keep the community safe through moderation, answer your questions, and report anonymous statistics about the archive. We do not sell personal data and we do not show advertising.
Every story and comment is checked by an AI system against the rules. A person on the admin team reviews anything it blocks, and you can ask why through “Ask Why”.

Published stories are public. If you post anonymously, your name and picture are not shown, but the admins can still see who posted. Private messages are seen by the people in the conversation; reported messages can be seen by admins. Original files, consent forms and ID numbers are never public.

Connections are encrypted. Files are stored encrypted, checked for viruses, and hidden location data is removed from photos. Admin accounts need a second sign-in step. Actions by admins are recorded in an audit log.

Your account and content stay until you delete them. A deleted story or account can be restored for 30 days and is then erased. Stories you posted “as told by” someone else, and testimonies given with consent, can be withdrawn at any time by asking the admins.

You can see, correct and download your data (My Profile › Download my data), delete your account (My Profile › Delete account), object to how your data is used, and complain to the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner.
You must be {n} or older to hold an account. Stories about anyone under 18 need the agreement of a parent or guardian, and children are not identified without it.
Cookies and storage on your device
The website uses one sign-in cookie, needed to keep you signed in, and stores your language, theme, drafts and offline copies of pages on your device. It uses no advertising or tracking cookies.
Questions about your data go to the admins through INBOX or the feedback form.
Anyone may read, listen to, search and cite the archive free of charge. To post, react, comment, message, follow or report you need an account, which you create by signing in with Google or Apple.

You keep the rights to what you post. By posting you allow the archive to store, display, translate, transcribe and preserve it, and to make it available to the public under the usage rights you choose for each story. Post only what you own or have permission to share.
If you share a story told to you by someone else, you confirm that they agreed. Either of you can ask for it to be withdrawn.
You agree to follow the Rules and netiquette. Content that breaks them may be blocked or removed, and accounts may be warned, suspended or deleted. You can always ask why.
Each story shows its usage rights. Respect them, and cite the archive when you use a story (every story has a “Cite” option). Downloads are offered only where the Contributor allows them.

If you believe something here copies your work or was posted without permission, use Report on the story or the feedback form, and say what it is and where the original is. The admins will review it and remove it if the report is right.
Stories describe personal experiences and are not official safety advice. The archive is not an emergency service: in an emergency, call the emergency numbers shown on the safety concern form.
